data.content_ref: inline:SRC_03 relies heavily on analogy to Design by Contract and Open-Closed reasoning to transfer per-element contract testing to the artifact-count problem, but its own disanalogies note that DbC 'typically targets object-level preconditions and postconditions' while the problem concerns a 'set-level invariant over dynamically growing committed evidence.' Rather than resolving this structural mismatch by identifying a published set-level testing principle, it leaves the transfer claim hanging on shared abstract structure. The problem asks which published testing principles support the property choice; an analogical bridge whose own disanalogies expose the central category gap (object-level vs. set-level) is not a grounded justification.
